architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added ijson>=3.2 as a new dependency to enable streaming JSON parsing
architecture_decisions.rationale: The ijson library provides incremental JSON parsing capabilities that allow processing large JSON files without loading the entire file into memory. This is essential for the memory optimization goal. The library is mature, well-maintained, and supports streaming parsing of JSON arrays, which matches the manifest file structure.
alternatives_considered: Other streaming JSON libraries like yajl-py

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Replaced monolithic json.load() calls with streaming ijson.items() generator
architecture_decisions.rationale: The original approach loaded entire manifest files (potentially gigabytes) into memory as Python lists/dicts. By using ijson.items(f, 'item'), we process JSON array items one at a time, significantly reducing peak memory usage. This is critical for large imports where manifest files can contain thousands of document records.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created iter_manifest_records() generator function to abstract streaming JSON parsing
architecture_decisions.rationale: Encapsulating the ijson streaming logic in a dedicated generator function provides a clean interface for iterating over manifest records. This abstraction hides implementation details, makes the code more readable, and centralizes error handling for JSON parsing issues. The function yields records one at a time, enabling memory-efficient processing.
alternatives_considered: Inline ijson calls throughout the code

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Changed from pre-loaded manifest list to on-demand streaming from manifest_paths
architecture_decisions.rationale: Instead of storing all manifest records in self.manifest list, we now store only file paths in self.manifest_paths and process records on-demand. This eliminates the large in-memory data structure. The approach maintains support for multiple manifest files (main manifest + split manifests) while processing them sequentially.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated error handling to use CommandError for JSON parsing failures and maintain test compatibility
architecture_decisions.rationale: Replaced json.decoder.JSONDecodeError with CommandError in the main parsing logic to maintain consistent error reporting. Updated tests to expect CommandError instead of JSONDecodeError. This ensures users get meaningful error messages while maintaining backward compatibility with existing error handling patterns.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented temporary file handling for decrypted manifests and proper cleanup
architecture_decisions.rationale: For encrypted imports, we now write decrypted records to temporary files (.decrypted.json) instead of modifying the original manifest in-place. This allows streaming decryption while maintaining the ability to process records sequentially. Added cleanup logic to delete temporary files after import completion.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained existing manifest file format and import workflow while changing internal processing
architecture_decisions.rationale: The external interface remains unchanged - manifest files still use the same JSON array format. All existing validation, decryption, and file copying logic works with the streaming approach. This ensures users can upgrade without changing their export/import processes.

implementation_summary:
The implementation transforms the document importer from a memory-intensive batch processor to a memory-efficient streaming processor. The key change is replacing json.load() with ijson.items() to parse JSON arrays incrementally. This eliminates the need to load entire manifest files (which can be gigabytes for large exports) into memory.

The approach maintains backward compatibility by keeping the same manifest file format and external API. A new iter_manifest_records() generator function abstracts the streaming logic, yielding records one at a time. For encrypted imports, the solution writes decrypted records to temporary files to enable streaming decryption while preserving the ability to process records sequentially.

The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing Django management command structure. All validation, file copying, and database loading logic now operates on streaming records rather than pre-loaded lists. Error handling was updated to use CommandError consistently, and tests were modified to reflect the new error propagation. The memory optimization is achieved without sacrificing functionality or requiring changes to export formats or user workflows.
